what: Which of the operator's instruction files reached the model in the baseline's isolated Claude Code and bridge arms. Counts and sizes only; no file content is stored here.

stub_check.method: Zero-quota check made after the baseline run, during review. The kit's fake Anthropic API (runner/lib/stub_anthropic.py) records each request a claude process makes; no model was called. Claude Code was started with the flag set the clean Claude Code arms used (below), once with the working directory under $HOME like the baseline workspaces (~/.cache/forge-ops/ccbench/tmp/...) and once outside $HOME. The request's first user message was searched for text of the operator's global instruction file and of the project instruction file at /home/floris/CLAUDE.md, plus three other markers that only occur in the global files.
stub_check.environment: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at the stub, a dummy ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1; default CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
stub_check.reading: With these flags Claude Code loads the CLAUDE.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md of every ancestor directory as project instructions. --setting-sources project does not stop that, so a workspace under $HOME receives the operator's global instructions. The Claude Code arms of suites a, b, c and d ran with workspaces under $HOME and therefore did too (the request itself was not captured during the baseline run).

bridge_transcripts.what: The `instructions` attachment of claude's own session transcripts for the bridged arms (results/runs/<run>/FB-*/seed1/transcripts/*/*.jsonl): which files were loaded as project instructions, and in how many of the 26 task transcripts of each arm.

forge_arms: Not captured. The Forge arms had a neutral .forge/AGENTS.md in every workspace. The static audit (PARITY.md, G3) records that Forge loads only the first non-empty instruction file and does not walk parent directories, which implies the FD arms did not receive either file; this was not verified with a request capture.
other_dimensions: The SWE-bench workspaces live under /var/tmp and the multi-turn workspaces under /tmp (the `workspace` field of the session records), both outside $HOME, so no ancestor instruction file applies to them. The SWE-bench Claude Code arm also ran with --safe-mode (swe/run.sh and the bin/claude shim of the kit).
